revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Moves
revealWordProblem.text: A group of friends are planning to make a movie. They research the running times of movies made. The data they collected are shown in the histogram. They have asked for your advice on how long their movie should run. What do you recommend? Explain your recommendation based on the data presented in the histogram.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A histogram titled Movie Running Times, with running time in minutes on the horizontal axis and frequency on the vertical axis.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Add up the histogram's frequencies: 7 + 30 + 39 + 22 + 12 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 114 movies total. The tallest bar is the 101–115 minute interval with 39 movies, the modal interval. A histogram groups values, so it does not reveal the exact mode of the ungrouped data. Combined with the neighboring 86–100 minute interval (30 movies), that's 30 + 39 = 69 of the 114 movies, or 69 ÷ 114 ≈ 0.605 = 60.5%, running between 86 and 115 minutes. Very few movies run longer than 145 minutes (2 + 1 + 1 = 4 movies, about 3.5%). Based on this data, I'd recommend the friends aim for a running time in the 101–115 minute range, since that's the most common length and keeps their movie in line with most movies made.

questions.stem: A histogram shows these frequencies: 0–4: 3 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 12 players, 15–19: 5 players. How many players are represented in total?
choiceFeedback: Did you count frequencies or find the highest value?
That total leaves out part of the data. Every bar contributes, so add all four frequencies together — including the shortest bar.
hints: The question asks for the TOTAL across all four intervals — not the tallest bar and not the biggest interval.
Each frequency counts the players in one interval, and no player is counted twice — so combine all four frequencies into one total.
Set up the addition: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. The sum of all the bar heights is the total number of players.
questions.stemEs: Un histograma muestra estas frecuencias: 0–4: 3 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 12 jugadores, 15–19: 5 jugadores. ¿Cuántos jugadores se representan en total?
hintsEs: La pregunta pide el TOTAL de los cuatro intervalos, no la barra más alta ni el intervalo más grande.
Cada frecuencia cuenta los jugadores de un intervalo, y ningún jugador se cuenta dos veces, así que combina las cuatro frecuencias en un solo total.
Plantea la suma: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. La suma de todas las alturas de las barras es el total de jugadores.

questions.stem: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The frequency (count) of data in that interval
The average of the data in that interval
questions.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.
choiceFeedback: A bar height is not something you calculate from the values — it is something you tally. Think about what you would count to make the bar taller.
Height shows how many—does it show the typical value?
Range is the interval spread, not the height.
hints: Think about what you'd count to draw one bar: you'd tally how many data values land inside that interval.
Height is a COUNT, not a calculation — no averaging, no middle values. Ask which choice simply says 'how many.'
First step: imagine the interval 10–14 holding the values 11, 12, 12, 14. Its bar would rise to 4 — because 4 values fall inside.
questions.stemEs: En un histograma, ¿qué representa la altura de cada barra?
questions.explanationEs: La altura de cada barra muestra la frecuencia: cuántos valores de datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
choicesEs: La frecuencia (el conteo) de datos en ese intervalo
El promedio de los datos de ese intervalo
hintsEs: Piensa qué contarías para dibujar una barra: contarías cuántos datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
La altura es un CONTEO, no un cálculo: sin promedios ni valores del medio. Pregunta qué opción simplemente dice 'cuántos'.
Primer paso: imagina el intervalo 10–14 con los valores 11, 12, 12, 14. Su barra llegaría a 4, porque 4 valores caen adentro.

questions.stem: How is a histogram different from a regular bar graph?
choices: Histogram bars touch (no gaps) because the intervals are continuous ranges
Histograms use colors and bar graphs don't
Bar graphs show numbers and histograms show words
questions.explanation: In a histogram, bars touch because each interval connects to the next (0–9, 10–19, etc.) — the data is continuous.
choiceFeedback: There is a real structural difference between the two graphs. Look at the spacing between the bars and at what the horizontal axis is measuring.
Histograms always show intervals—this is the key difference.
Colors don't define a histogram—structure does.
hints: Picture both graphs side by side: one has spaces between its bars, one doesn't. Ask why that would be.
Think about the x-axis: categories like 'red, blue, green' can be separated, but number intervals like 0–9 and 10–19 connect end to end.
First step: write two neighboring intervals, 0–9 and 10–19. Notice that 10 starts right where 9 ends — that's why the bars behave differently.
questions.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia un histograma de una gráfica de barras común?
questions.explanationEs: En un histograma las barras se tocan porque cada intervalo se conecta con el siguiente (0–9, 10–19, etc.): los datos son continuos.
choicesEs: Las barras del histograma se tocan (sin espacios) porque los intervalos son rangos continuos
Los histogramas usan colores y las gráficas de barras no
Las gráficas de barras muestran números y los histogramas muestran palabras
hintsEs: Imagina las dos gráficas lado a lado: una tiene espacios entre las barras y la otra no. Pregunta por qué sería así.
Piensa en el eje x: categorías como 'rojo, azul, verde' se pueden separar, pero intervalos numéricos como 0–9 y 10–19 se conectan de punta a punta.
Primer paso: escribe dos intervalos vecinos, 0–9 y 10–19. Nota que el 10 empieza justo donde termina el 9: por eso las barras se comportan distinto.

steps: 1. Set equal intervals along the horizontal axis with no gaps
2. Count the frequency (how many data values fall into each interval)
3. Draw adjacent bars with heights equal to frequency
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Display Data: Histograms is counting a boundary value in two intervals at once — for example, putting the value 10 in both the '0–9' bin and the '10–19' bin. Each data value belongs to exactly ONE interval. Before you submit, add up all your frequencies and check that the total matches the number of data values you started with.

level1.stem: Data: 1, 4, 12, 13, 17, 25. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19 and 20–29. What is the frequency of 0–9?

hints: Count the values from 0 to 9.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores de 0 a 9.
level1.explanation: Find the values from 0 to 9: 1, 4 Count them: 2 values
level1.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 0 a 9: 1, 4 Cuéntalos: 2 valores

level1.stem: A histogram has bars 0–9: 5, 10–19: 2 and 20–29: 3. How many values are there in all?
level1.stemEs: Un histograma tiene las barras 0–9: 5, 10–19: 2 y 20–29: 3. ¿Cuántos valores hay en total?
hints: Each bar height is a count. Add the heights.
hintsEs: La altura de cada barra es un conteo. Suma las alturas.
level1.explanation: Read each bar height: 5, 2, 3 Add the heights: 5 + 2 + 3 = 10
level1.explanationEs: Lee la altura de cada barra: 5, 2, 3 Suma las alturas: 5 + 2 + 3 = 10

level1.stem: Data: 7, 15, 21, 22, 26, 28. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19 and 20–29. What is the frequency of 20–29?
level1.stemEs: Datos: 7, 15, 21, 22, 26, 28. Usa intervalos de 0–9, 10–19 y 20–29. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 20–29?
hints: Count the values from 20 to 29.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores de 20 a 29.
level1.explanation: Find the values from 20 to 29: 21, 22, 26, 28 Count them: 4 values
level1.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 20 a 29: 21, 22, 26, 28 Cuéntalos: 4 valores

level1.stem: Data: 2, 5, 13, 16, 18, 21. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19 and 20–29. What is the frequency of 10–19?
level1.stemEs: Datos: 2, 5, 13, 16, 18, 21. Usa intervalos de 0–9, 10–19 y 20–29. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 10–19?
hints: Frequency means how many values. Count the values from 10 to 19.
hintsEs: Frecuencia significa cuántos valores. Cuenta los valores de 10 a 19.
level1.explanation: Find the values from 10 to 19: 13, 16, 18 Count them: 3 values
level1.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 10 a 19: 13, 16, 18 Cuéntalos: 3 valores

level1.stem: Ten players scored these points per game: 4, 8, 12, 15, 17, 19, 22, 26, 31, 34. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19, 20–29 and 30–39. How tall is the 10–19 bar?
level1.stemEs: Diez jugadores anotaron estos puntos por partido: 4, 8, 12, 15, 17, 19, 22, 26, 31, 34. Usa intervalos de 0–9, 10–19, 20–29 y 30–39. ¿Qué altura tiene la barra 10–19?
hints: The height of a bar is the number of values in its interval.
hintsEs: La altura de una barra es la cantidad de valores en su intervalo.
level1.explanation: Find the values from 10 to 19: 12, 15, 17, 19 Count them. That is the bar height: 4 values → height 4
level1.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 10 a 19: 12, 15, 17, 19 Cuéntalos. Esa es la altura de la barra: 4 valores → altura 4

level2.stem: Kim makes a histogram of 4, 10, 15, 19, 20, 27. She says the 10–19 bar has a height of 4. She counted 10, 15, 19 and 20. What is the correct height?
level2.stemEs: Kim hace un histograma de 4, 10, 15, 19, 20, 27. Dice que la barra 10–19 tiene una altura de 4. Contó 10, 15, 19 y 20. ¿Cuál es la altura correcta?
hints: Look at each value Kim counted. Is every one from 10 to 19?
hintsEs: Mira cada valor que contó Kim. ¿Está cada uno entre 10 y 19?
level2.explanation: Check each value Kim counted: 20 is not in 10–19 Count only 10 to 19: 10, 15, 19 → 3
level2.explanationEs: Revisa cada valor que contó Kim: 20 no está en 10–19 Cuenta solo de 10 a 19: 10, 15, 19 → 3

level2.stem: Data: 19, 20, 20, 21, 29, 30, 38. Use intervals of 10–19, 20–29 and 30–39. What is the frequency of 20–29?
level2.stemEs: Datos: 19, 20, 20, 21, 29, 30, 38. Usa intervalos de 10–19, 20–29 y 30–39. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 20–29?
hints: Watch the edges. 19 and 30 are not in 20–29.
hintsEs: Cuidado con los bordes. El 19 y el 30 no están en 20–29.
level2.explanation: Find the values from 20 to 29: 20, 20, 21, 29 Count them: 4 values
level2.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 20 a 29: 20, 20, 21, 29 Cuéntalos: 4 valores

level2.stem: Data: 6, 7, 11, 18, 24, 25, 29. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19 and 20–29. What is the frequency of 20–29?
level2.stemEs: Datos: 6, 7, 11, 18, 24, 25, 29. Usa intervalos de 0–9, 10–19 y 20–29. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 20–29?
hints: Count the values from 20 to 29.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores de 20 a 29.
level2.explanation: Find the values from 20 to 29: 24, 25, 29 Count them: 3 values
level2.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 20 a 29: 24, 25, 29 Cuéntalos: 3 valores

level2.stem: A histogram shows 30 players' points per game. 0–9 has 6 players, 10–19 has 11, 20–29 is missing and 30–39 has 4. What is the frequency of 20–29?
level2.stemEs: Un histograma muestra los puntos por partido de 30 jugadores. 0–9 tiene 6 jugadores, 10–19 tiene 11, falta 20–29 y 30–39 tiene 4. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 20–29?
hints: All the bars together must add to 30 players.
hintsEs: Todas las barras juntas deben sumar 30 jugadores.
level2.explanation: Add the bars you know: 6 + 11 + 4 = 21 Subtract from the total: 30 − 21 = 9
level2.explanationEs: Suma las barras que conoces: 6 + 11 + 4 = 21 Resta del total: 30 − 21 = 9

level2.stem: A histogram shows the ages of people at a pool. 0–19 has 12 people, 20–39 has 9 people and 40–59 has 4 people. How many people are at the pool?
level2.stemEs: Un histograma muestra las edades de las personas en una piscina. 0–19 tiene 12 personas, 20–39 tiene 9 personas y 40–59 tiene 4 personas. ¿Cuántas personas hay en la piscina?
hints: Each bar counts people. Add all the bar heights.
hintsEs: Cada barra cuenta personas. Suma las alturas de todas las barras.
level2.explanation: Read each bar height: 12, 9, 4 Add the heights: 12 + 9 + 4 = 25
level2.explanationEs: Lee la altura de cada barra: 12, 9, 4 Suma las alturas: 12 + 9 + 4 = 25

level3.stem: A histogram uses intervals 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, and 30–39. A data value of 19 belongs in which interval?
choiceFeedback: 19 is larger than 9, so it cannot sit in that bar. Read the upper bound of each interval.
That interval starts at 20, and 19 is below it. The 10-19 interval includes its endpoint.
Histogram intervals are built so they never overlap, so every value lands in exactly one bar.
level3.explanation: 19 falls between 10 and 19 inclusive, so it belongs in the 10–19 bar. Intervals must not overlap, so every value lands in exactly one.

level3.stem: A histogram has bars 0–9: 4, 10–19: 6 and 20–29: 2. Which statement must be true?
level3.stemEs: Un histograma tiene las barras 0–9: 4, 10–19: 6 y 20–29: 2. ¿Qué enunciado tiene que ser verdadero?
hints: A histogram shows counts. Does it show the exact values?
hintsEs: Un histograma muestra conteos. ¿Muestra los valores exactos?
level3.explanation: Read what the 10–19 bar says: height 6 → 6 values from 10 to 19 Check what a bar cannot tell: no exact values
level3.explanationEs: Lee lo que dice la barra 10–19: altura 6 → 6 valores de 10 a 19 Revisa lo que una barra no puede decir: no da valores exactos
choiceFeedback: A bar does not show exact values. The 6 values could be any numbers from 10 to 19.
29 is the end of the interval. The greatest value could be anywhere from 20 to 29.
There are 3 bars, not 3 values. The bars add to 4 + 6 + 2 = 12 values.

level3.stem: Data: 8, 10, 13, 19, 20, 26, 30, 30. Use intervals of 0–9, 10–19, 20–29 and 30–39. What is the frequency of 10–19?
level3.stemEs: Datos: 8, 10, 13, 19, 20, 26, 30, 30. Usa intervalos de 0–9, 10–19, 20–29 y 30–39. ¿Cuál es la frecuencia de 10–19?
hints: 10 and 19 are in 10–19. 20 is not.
hintsEs: El 10 y el 19 están en 10–19. El 20 no.
level3.explanation: Find the values from 10 to 19: 10, 13, 19 Count them: 3 values
level3.explanationEs: Busca los valores de 10 a 19: 10, 13, 19 Cuéntalos: 3 valores

level3.stem: A histogram shows the weights of 40 dogs in pounds. 0–19 has 14 dogs, 20–39 has 15, 40–59 has 8 and 60–79 has 3. How many dogs weigh 40 pounds or more?
level3.stemEs: Un histograma muestra los pesos de 40 perros en libras. 0–19 tiene 14 perros, 20–39 tiene 15, 40–59 tiene 8 y 60–79 tiene 3. ¿Cuántos perros pesan 40 libras o más?
hints: Which bars start at 40 or more?
hintsEs: ¿Qué barras empiezan en 40 o más?
level3.explanation: Find the bars for 40 or more: 40–59 and 60–79 Add their heights: 8 + 3 = 11
level3.explanationEs: Busca las barras de 40 o más: 40–59 y 60–79 Suma sus alturas: 8 + 3 = 11

level3.stem: Data: 2, 4, 6, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17. With intervals of 10, the 10–19 bar is 5 tall. Now use intervals of 5. How tall is the 10–14 bar?
level3.stemEs: Datos: 2, 4, 6, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17. Con intervalos de 10, la barra 10–19 mide 5. Ahora usa intervalos de 5. ¿Qué altura tiene la barra 10–14?
hints: The 10–19 bar splits into two bars: 10–14 and 15–19.
hintsEs: La barra 10–19 se divide en dos barras: 10–14 y 15–19.
level3.explanation: Split the 10–19 values: 10–14: 11, 12, 13, 14; 15–19: 17 Count the 10–14 values: 4 values Check that the two bars add to 5: 4 + 1 = 5
level3.explanationEs: Divide los valores de 10–19: 10–14: 11, 12, 13, 14; 15–19: 17 Cuenta los valores de 10–14: 4 valores Comprueba que las dos barras suman 5: 4 + 1 = 5

steps.say: About 60% of movies run 86 to 115 minutes.

workedSteps.answer: Aim for a running time of 101–115 minutes, the most common length.
